newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Bear Stearns sees strong 2nd-half Brazil growth.
newsitem.headline: Bear Stearns sees strong 2nd-half Brazil growth.

text.p: Brazil's economy is poised for strong second-half growth as longer debt maturities and lower barriers to foreign access to its debt markets quickly reduce interest rates, Bear Stearns said.
"We expect Brazil to grow strongly in the second half of 1997," Bear Stearns analysts David Malpass and Elizabeth Olson said in a report.

"Brazil has embarked on a very positive process to reduce interest rates, reduce financial risk, improve the fiscal deficit and create a higher sustainable growth rate by efficiently accessing imported capital," they wrote.
The analysts said Brazil took measures last August to slow 1997's growth rate but added they disagree with the view that credit controls imposed this April and May were meant to slow growth.

"They were rifle shots, with the brunt born by imports," they said. "The government is now ready to see growth rise steadily above the 4.2 percent first-quarter rate. Industrial production was up eight percent in April year-on-year."

The recent trends of longer debt maturities and lower barriers to foreign participation "should have a positive impact on the economy, interest rates and the availability of financing for smaller companies," Malpass and Olson said.
Longer debt maturities should lower the risk to the issuer and set the stage for lower interest rates, which will in turn quickly reduce Brazil's fiscal deficit, they said.
"This will add to the perception of declining risk, creating a virtuous circle," they added.
